strings.l:free: Free, no ads, no tracking. Files come from the official VideoLAN servers.
strings.l:lead: VLC is a free and open source cross-platform multimedia player that plays most multimedia files, DVDs, Audio CDs, VCDs and streaming protocols.

strings.o:a_p: VideoLAN started as a student project in Paris and grew into one of the largest open source multimedia communities in the world. Today it is run by volunteers and a small board, funded by donations and partners, and accountable to no one but its users.
strings.o:desc: VideoLAN is the non-profit behind VLC media player and a family of open source multimedia projects: dav1d, x264, libVLC, libdvdcss, libbluray, DVBlast and more.

strings.o:f_x264: The most popular software video encoder in the world, behind a huge share of online video.

strings.o:nw_news-2026-07-15_x: New releases of libdvdcss (1.6.0) and libdvdread (7.1) have been published today. The biggest features of those releases are related to recordable DVD media (DVD-VR) , including CPRM decryption, continuing the DVD-Audio…

strings.o:nw_news-2026-09-22_x: VLC 3.0.24 is a major security update, with over 130 security fixes across VLC and its bundled libraries. It upgrades FFmpeg from 4.4 to 8.1.2 and updates 49 third-party libraries. New features include ATRAC decoding,…
strings.o:p_h: Much more than a media player
strings.o:p_p: VLC is the best known, but VideoLAN maintains {n} open source projects: codecs, disc libraries and broadcast tools that power browsers, operating systems, streaming services and TV networks.
strings.o:pe_p: {n} named contributors in code, translation, artwork and documentation, from more than 40 countries, meeting every year at the VideoLAN Dev Days.
strings.o:st_p: Even if you have never opened VLC, chances are VideoLAN code decoded, encoded or carried the last video you watched. Here is how the pieces fit together.
strings.o:t1996_d: Students at École Centrale Paris start VideoLAN to stream video across the campus network.
strings.o:t1998_d: The code is rewritten from scratch, laying the foundations of today’s VLC.
strings.o:t2001_d: On 1 February, the École agrees to release everything under the GNU GPL.
strings.o:t2004_d: Work starts on x264, which becomes the reference H.264 encoder.
strings.o:t2008_d: The community meets in Paris for the first VideoLAN Dev Days.
strings.o:t2009_d: VideoLAN separates from the École and is run by its own non-profit.
strings.o:t2011_d: The engine is relicensed so any app, free or not, can embed it.
strings.o:t2012_d: A Kickstarter raises £47,056 to bring VLC to Windows 8, RT and Phone.
strings.o:t2013_d: VLC for iOS returns to the App Store, free in every country.
strings.o:t2016_d: VLC arrives on the living-room screen.
strings.o:t2017_d: VideoLAN joins the Alliance for Open Media to build a royalty-free codec.
strings.o:t2018_d: The AV1 decoder starts with the FFmpeg community and soon ships in browsers.
strings.o:t2021_d: Two decades of free software and more than 3.5 billion downloads.
strings.o:t2025_d: At CES, VideoLAN demos on-device subtitle generation and translation for VLC 4.0.
strings.o:t2026_d: The 15th Dev Days in Rome, VLC {v} with 130+ security fixes, and 7 billion downloads.
